timeline.title: Cameroon Secures First Women's Africa Cup of Nations Title with Victory Over Malawi
timeline.summary: Cameroon triumphed over Malawi 3-0 in the final of the Women's Africa Cup of Nations, marking their first title in the tournament's history. Marie Ngah Manga scored two goals, while Naomi Eto added another. This victory comes after Cameroon had previously lost in three finals, all against Nigeria. Both teams, along with Morocco and Algeria, have qualified for the upcoming Women's World Cup in Brazil.

event_overview.title: About Women's Africa Cup of Nations
event_overview.subject: Women's Africa Cup of Nations
event_overview.summary: The Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) is the Confederation of African Football’s continental championship for African women’s senior national teams. Morocco 2026 is an expanded edition of the competition and also serves as CAF’s qualifying route for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The official match schedule set the tournament from 26 July to 16 August 2026, with the final in Rabat on 16 August.

facts.label: Host and venues
facts.value: Morocco hosted the tournament, with matches scheduled in Rabat and Casablanca.

facts.label: Organizer
facts.value: The competition is organized by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), Africa’s football governing body, in conjunction with a local organizing committee for this edition.

facts.label: Participants and format
facts.value: Sixteen national teams competed for the first time, divided into four groups of four; the leading teams progressed to a knockout phase culminating in the final.

facts.label: World Cup qualification role
facts.value: The four WAFCON semi-finalists qualify directly for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil, while the losing quarter-finalists play for two CAF places in the FIFA Play-Off Tournament.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline provides a general orientation and a championship-outcome development, rather than a match-by-match account, complete results archive, or broader history of WAFCON.
